verdict: A quiet, compact bedroom purifier with Wi-Fi, a PM2.5 sensor and a carbon layer for smells.
pros: Wi-Fi control and schedules in the Air+ app
PM2.5 sensor with numerical display
Very quiet in Sleep mode (about 20 dB)
Carbon layer helps with cooking smells
cons: CADR of 250 m³/h limits it to bedrooms and small living rooms
Replacement filter costs more than the AC0920's
skipIf: your room is bigger than about 250 sq ft

name: Philips AC0920 Air Purifier (900 Series)
verdict: The no-fuss version of the AC0950: same airflow and quiet sleep mode, without Wi-Fi.
pros: CADR of 250 m³/h for bedrooms up to about 200–250 sq ft
Real-time air quality light and auto mode
Quiet Sleep mode at about 20 dB
Cheaper replacement filter than the AC0950
cons: No carbon layer, so weak on smells and gases
skipIf: you cook near the bedroom or want app control

name: Honeywell Air Touch V1
verdict: A small, low-power purifier that does the basics for a compact bedroom, study or home office.
pros: Very low power draw (12 W)
H13 HEPA with carbon in a small footprint
Quiet on low speed (29 dB)
Rated filter life of about 9,000 hours
cons: CADR of 152 m³/h is only enough for small rooms
No air quality sensor or auto mode
skipIf: your room is over about 150 sq ft or you live in a city with severe winter smog
